close_reason: Affirmative review finding — verified in-source. The lint deny is at memory.rs:183 and lib.rs:159; the explanatory rustdoc unit defending why std::sync::Mutex (not tokio's) is correct, and what to do if a future change needs to .await inside the critical section, is at memory.rs:149-180 (the whole '# Concurrency' section). The lint + rationale pair is intact and self-documenting. No code change is warranted — the bead documents the convention is correct and load-bearing, and the in-source rustdoc already provides the durable defense.
description:
memory.rs:65-66 and lib.rs:123 both have:

    #![deny(clippy::await_holding_lock)]    // or #[deny(...)] at module scope

This is the workspace's enforcement that MemoryBackend's std::sync::Mutex (memory.rs:69) is never held across an .await point. If a future change introduces an .await while a guard is held, clippy fails compilation. Without the lint, the bug would be silent in tests (single-task runtime) and would only surface in production multi-task workloads as deadlocks.

memory.rs rustdoc at lines 57-63 reinforces the invariant with a 'switch to tokio::sync::Mutex' fallback path, so when the lint fires the fix is mechanical and discoverable.

Defend against: 'this lint is too restrictive', 'we can hold the lock across an await as long as we drop it before yielding'. No, you can't — clippy::await_holding_lock catches the exact future-state shape where the lock guard outlives the .await even if drop is in scope. The lint exists because the bug is non-obvious.

Adjacent: same pattern in jmap-chat-server (tracked as bd:JMAP-x2gd.26) and presumably the canonical jmap-mail-server. Workspace-wide invariant.

This is the second cookie-cutter decision worth preserving against simplification pressure. Anyone touching the lock impl should see the lint and understand WHY it's there — the comment block above the deny attribute explains, succinctly: 'no lock guard is held across an .await'. Preserve the deny + comment as a unit.
title: Module-wide #![deny(clippy::await_holding_lock)] is correct concurrency invariant
